claims.claim: For d=δ⁺(D)≥1, a directed cycle of length at least d+1 can be found in polynomial time; additionally, n<d+k is an immediate sound NO condition. Thus the target is completely solved for k=1.
claims.evidence: For a maximal simple directed path v₁…v_p, every out-neighbor of v_p lies among v₁,…,v_{p−1}. If v_i is its earliest out-neighbor, the d distinct out-neighbors occupy positions i through p−1, so p−i≥d. Hence v_i…v_pv_i is a cycle of length p−i+1≥d+1. Greedy extension is polynomial. Since every cycle has at most n vertices, n<d+k is soundly NO. A 2-strong input has d≥1, so this constructs the required cycle when k=1.
claims.witness: The maximal-path algorithm outputs the cycle v_i→v_{i+1}→⋯→v_p→v_i.
claims.search_method: Independent maximal-path proof, supplemented by exhaustive checking of every loopless digraph on two through four vertices; no web or external material used.

claims.claim: For any integer L≥2, existence of a directed cycle of length at least L is exactly equivalent to a short-leg two-way linkage, yielding an explicit O(n^L(n+m)) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: If an enumerated simple L-vertex path v₁…v_L has a v_L-to-v₁ path after deleting v₂,…,v_{L−1}, a shortest such return path is simple and intersects the first path only at its endpoints, so their union is a simple directed cycle of length at least L. Conversely, L consecutive vertices of any cycle of length at least L form such a path, with the complementary cycle segment supplying the return path. There are at most n^L tuples, and each reachability test costs O(n+m), giving the stated bound after immediately rejecting L>n.
claims.witness: Take any L consecutive vertices of a qualifying cycle and its complementary directed segment; in the reverse direction, concatenate an enumerated leg with a shortest return path.
claims.search_method: Proved both implications and checked them exhaustively for all loopless digraphs of order at most four and all 2≤L≤n.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially checkable upper-bound certificate: if X is an independent vertex set and every arc entering X from outside X has its tail in S⊆V(D)\X, then every directed cycle has length at most n−|X|+|S|.
claims.evidence: For every x∈C∩X, independence forces its predecessor on C outside X, and the entry condition places that predecessor in S. Different x have different predecessors because each cycle vertex has one successor. Thus |C∩X|≤|C∩S|≤|S|, while at most n−|X| vertices of C lie outside X. This proves |C|≤n−|X|+|S|. Independence and the entering-arc condition are directly checkable in polynomial time.
claims.witness: The injective map x↦pred_C(x) from C∩X into C∩S is the certificate-counting witness.
claims.search_method: Independent injection proof plus exhaustive enumeration of all valid X,S certificates in every loopless digraph of order at most four.

claims.claim: Let D be a bidirected complete multipartite digraph on n vertices, and let d=δ⁺(D). Its circumference is exactly min(n,2d), and a maximum directed cycle can be constructed in polynomial time. If d≥2, then D is 2-strong.
claims.evidence: If the largest part has size M, then d=n−M. On any cycle its vertices must be separated by vertices outside that part, so c(D)≤min(n,2d). If M>d, alternating all d outside vertices with d vertices from the largest part attains 2d. If M≤d, distribute every other part injectively among M gaps between the largest-part vertices; because each part has size at most M and there are at least M outside vertices, all gaps can be made nonempty, with no repeated part inside a gap. This yields a Hamiltonian cycle. The construction is polynomial. When d≥2, deletion of any one vertex leaves at least two nonempty parts, and bidirected cross-arcs make the remainder strong.
claims.witness: The maximum cycle is the alternating 2d-cycle when M>d and the gap-distribution Hamiltonian cycle when M≤d.
claims.search_method: Derived both upper bounds and both constructive equality cases, then exhaustively checked 85 small multipartite instances.

claims.claim: The target has a polynomial-time solution on bidirected complete multipartite digraphs: such an input is YES exactly when n≥d+k and d≥k.
claims.evidence: Using c(D)=min(n,2d), a target cycle exists exactly when min(n,2d)≥d+k. This is equivalent to n≥d+k and 2d≥d+k, with the second inequality equivalent to d≥k. The constructive equality proof for the circumference outputs a qualifying cycle in polynomial time whenever both conditions hold.
claims.witness: The condition pair is obtained by splitting min(n,2d)≥d+k; the cycle from claim 3 is the output witness.
claims.search_method: Checked the integer-inequality equivalence and the constructive dependence on the verified circumference formula; finite instances were also checked exactly.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥3 there are 2-strong NO-instances of arbitrarily large order satisfying n≥d+k: the bidirected complete bipartite digraph with part sizes 2 and a, for any a≥k, has d=2 and circumference 4=d+2.
claims.evidence: In bidirected K_{2,a}, vertices in the a-part have outdegree 2 and those in the 2-part have outdegree a, so d=2. A directed cycle alternates between the parts and therefore uses at most two vertices from each; a directed 4-cycle exists, so c(D)=4. Since both parts remain nonempty after any one-vertex deletion, the remainder is strong. For a≥k≥3, n=a+2≥d+k while c(D)=4<d+k, and unbounded a gives unbounded order.
claims.witness: For distinct large-part vertices u,v and the two small-part vertices x,y, x→u→y→v→x is a longest cycle.
claims.search_method: Direct degree, alternation, and one-vertex-deletion analysis, with small complete multipartite instances checked exhaustively.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥4 there are 2-strong NO-instances with arbitrarily large minimum outdegree and with n≥d+k; indeed their circumference is exactly d+3.
claims.evidence: In the two-gateway construction, Q\{x,y} has outdegree q−1, A has outdegree q, and x,y have outdegree q−1+a, hence d=q−1. Deleting one vertex leaves a nonempty bidirected core and at least one gateway, so all remaining vertices mutually reach one another. Every cycle vertex in A must be preceded by x or y, giving at most two A-vertices and c(D)≤q+2=d+3. The displayed cycle using both gateways, two A-vertices, and every core vertex attains q+2. Taking a≥k−1 gives n=q+a≥d+k, while k≥4 makes d+3<d+k; letting q grow makes d unbounded.
claims.witness: For Q\{x,y}={z₁,…,z_{q−2}}, the cycle x→a₁→z₁→⋯→z_{q−2}→y→a₂→x has length q+2.
claims.search_method: Direct symbolic degree, connectivity, predecessor, and cycle-construction proof; bounded gateway instances were exhaustively checked.

claims.claim: The two-gateway example extends exactly as follows. For integers s≥2, q≥s+1, and a≥s, let Q be a bidirected q-vertex clique, let A be an independent a-vertex set, add every arc A→Q, and add arcs from Q to A precisely when their tail belongs to a fixed s-set S⊂Q. Then d=q−1, the strong vertex-connectivity is exactly s, and the circumference is q+s=d+s+1.
claims.evidence: Because Q\S is nonempty, its vertices attain the minimum outdegree q−1; A-vertices have outdegree q and gateways have q−1+a. After deleting fewer than s vertices, at least one gateway, one A-vertex, and core vertices survive; A reaches Q directly and Q reaches A through the surviving gateway, so the remainder is strong. Removing all S leaves nonempty Q\S and A with no Q\S-to-A path, proving connectivity exactly s. Each A-vertex on a cycle has a distinct predecessor in S, so at most s occur and c(D)≤q+s. The explicit alternating gateway/A segment followed by all of Q\S attains q+s.
claims.witness: For S={s₁,…,s_s} and distinct a₁,…,a_s∈A, use s₁→a₁→s₂→a₂→⋯→s_s→a_s, then traverse every vertex of Q\S and return to s₁.
claims.search_method: Independently proved the lower and upper connectivity bounds and circumference equality; exact enumeration checked 15 bounded parameter instances.

claims.claim: For every k≥3 and h≥0 there is a 2-strong NO-instance whose order and circumference satisfy n=d+k+h and c(D)=d+k−1. For every k≥4 these instances can additionally have arbitrarily large d and strong vertex-connectivity exactly k−2.
claims.evidence: For k=3, bidirected K_{2,3+h} has d=2, n=5+h=d+k+h, and c=4=d+k−1. For k≥4, substitute s=k−2, a=k−1+h, and any q≥k−1 into the verified gateway family. Then d=q−1, n=q+a=d+k+h, connectivity is s=k−2≥2, and c=q+s=d+k−1. Thus every instance is 2-strong and NO, while q can grow without bound for fixed k,h, making d arbitrarily large.
claims.witness: The stated K_{2,3+h} and the gateway parameters (s,a,q)=(k−2,k−1+h,q) are explicit witnesses for every quantified k,h.
claims.search_method: Checked both parameter regimes by exact substitution into independently verified constructions; integer identities were also exercised over ranges of k,h,q.

claims.claim: The target has a polynomial-time solution on semicomplete digraphs: such an input is YES exactly when n≥d+k, and a Hamiltonian directed cycle can be constructed when YES.
claims.evidence: Let C be a non-Hamiltonian cycle in a strong semicomplete digraph. If an outside z cannot be inserted between consecutive vertices, then either every vertex of C sends to z and z sends to none of C, or the reverse: one arc C→z propagates around C under the no-insertion condition, while absence of every such arc gives the reverse orientation by semicompleteness. If no outside vertex is insertable, strongness forces both strict classes and a directed arc u→v from the C-dominated class to the C-dominating class. Then any edge c_i→c_{i+1} can be replaced by c_i→u→v→c_{i+1}. Repeated single- or double-vertex insertions construct a Hamiltonian cycle polynomially. Therefore a target cycle exists exactly when its requested length d+k does not exceed n.
claims.witness: At each iteration insert z using c_i→z→c_{i+1}, or insert a class-transition pair using c_i→u→v→c_{i+1}.
claims.search_method: Completed the insertion proof from first principles and exhaustively verified Hamiltonicity of all 52,528 strong semicomplete digraphs of orders two through five.

claims.claim: Given any baseline cycle C with ℓ=|C|≥d+1, either ℓ≥d+k and C is a target witness, or r=d+k−ℓ satisfies 1≤r≤k−1 and the target reduces exactly to Connected Assignment Augmentation: find a perfect matching whose induced permutation has exactly one nontrivial cycle and at least ℓ+r nonfixed vertices.
claims.evidence: A perfect matching maps every left vertex u to one distinct right vertex π(u), hence defines a permutation. Its nonfixed permutation cycles use precisely digraph arcs and are directed cycles; fixed points use the artificial zero-weight diagonals. Exactly one nontrivial permutation cycle therefore corresponds bijectively to one directed cycle, and its number of nonfixed vertices is its length. Conversely, extend any directed cycle's successor assignment by diagonals. The threshold ℓ+r equals d+k. If ℓ<d+k, integrality gives r≥1, and ℓ≥d+1 gives r=d+k−ℓ≤k−1. The construction and witness transfer are polynomial.
claims.witness: The baseline cycle's successor edges plus diagonals form the incumbent matching; any qualifying target cycle gives, and is recovered from, the matching's unique nontrivial permutation cycle.
claims.search_method: Proved the matching/permutation bijection and both inequalities for r; exhaustively compared one-cycle matching weights with all cycle lengths on small digraphs.

claims.claim: For every loopless digraph D, the maximum number p(D) of vertices coverable by pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles is computable in polynomial time by maximum-weight bipartite perfect matching. Moreover c(D)≤p(D), so p(D)<d+k is a sound polynomial-time NO rule.
claims.evidence: Every perfect matching in the arc-plus-diagonal bipartite graph is a permutation. Its nonfixed components are pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles, and every associated edge has weight one, so its weight is their total number of vertices. Conversely, any directed-cycle packing extends with diagonal edges to a perfect matching of the same weight. Thus maximum matching weight is exactly p(D), computable polynomially. Any single cycle is a packing, hence c(D)≤p(D), making p(D)<d+k a sound rejection condition.
claims.witness: Complete a maximum cycle packing with zero-weight diagonal matches on every uncovered vertex; the inverse witness is the collection of nonfixed permutation cycles.
claims.search_method: Established the two-way weight-preserving correspondence and exhaustively enumerated assignments and cycle packings for every loopless digraph of order at most four.

claims.claim: The cycle-packing bound subsumes every independent-set predecessor certificate from the parent: p(D)≤n−|X|+|S| under that certificate's hypotheses. It is tight on the parent's bidirected complete multipartite, gateway, and strong semicomplete families.
claims.evidence: Across a vertex-disjoint cycle packing, map every covered x∈X to its predecessor. Independence places that predecessor outside X, the entry hypothesis places it in S, and disjointness plus unique successors makes the map injective. Hence at most |S| covered vertices lie in X and at most n−|X| outside, proving p(D)≤n−|X|+|S|. For multipartite graphs, a largest part X and S=V\X give p≤2d when 2d<n, attained by the 2d-cycle; otherwise the Hamiltonian cycle gives p=n. For gateways, X=A and the gateway set S give p≤q+s, attained by the displayed cycle. Strong semicomplete digraphs are Hamiltonian, so p=c=n.
claims.witness: The predecessor injection proves subsumption; the maximum cycles constructed in the three families are packings attaining each corresponding upper bound.
claims.search_method: Extended the predecessor argument across disjoint cycles and checked every equality case symbolically; exhaustive small-graph tests also verified the packing inequality for every valid X,S.

claims.claim: The one-cycle constraint cannot be discarded even for 2-strong inputs: the bidirected Petersen digraph has d=3 and p(D)=10 but circumference c(D)=9. Consequently, for k=7 it is a NO-instance with n=d+k on which the matching relaxation attains the target threshold.
claims.evidence: Bidirection makes every outdegree three. Deleting an outer vertex leaves the inner 5-cycle connecting all remaining outer vertices through spokes; deleting an inner vertex gives the symmetric argument, so every one-vertex deletion is strong. Five spoke digons cover all ten vertices, proving p=10. A Hamiltonian cycle would cross the outer/inner cut an even positive number of times, hence use two or four spokes. With two, each side must be a spanning path: its spoke indices must differ by ±1 on the outer 5-cycle and ±2 on the inner 5-cycle, impossible modulo five. With four and omitted spoke t, degree constraints force two disjoint 5-cycles rather than one Hamiltonian cycle. The displayed 9-cycle proves c=9. Thus d+7=10=n, while no length-10 cycle exists and p reaches 10.
claims.witness: With indices modulo five, a₁→a₂→a₃→a₄→b₄→b₂→b₀→b₃→b₁→a₁ is a 9-cycle; the five spoke 2-cycles form a packing of size ten.
claims.search_method: Independently checked connectivity, the spoke-parity obstruction, the forced four-spoke case, and the explicit witnesses; exact cycle enumeration returned circumference 9 and packing witness size 10.

target_evidence: The source target requires an f(k)n^{O(1)} algorithm for arbitrary 2-strong digraphs. The draft supplies no such algorithm: its exact linkage algorithm has exponent d+k, and Connected Assignment Augmentation is only an exact reformulation with no FPT method for enforcing one nontrivial cycle. It also does not settle k=2. Nevertheless, the verified k=1 algorithm, exact polynomial special-class algorithms, upper-bound rules, obstruction families, and assignment/packing reformulations are material correct progress. The writeup expressly calls the resolution partial and identifies the missing general FPT step, so it does not overclaim target coverage.
checks_performed: Read only /evidence/source.json and /evidence/parent.json as evidence; used no web, retrieval database, receipt, other arm, prior run, or other solution.
Recomputed the SHA-256 of all 14 claim strings; every value matched its supplied claim_sha256.

Independently reconstructed the maximal-path, linkage, predecessor, multipartite, gateway, semicomplete-insertion, assignment, packing, and Petersen arguments, including all parameter substitutions and boundary cases.

Created and ran /work/tcs_attempt4_exact_checker.py; it returned PASS after checking all 4,164 loopless digraphs of orders 2–4, 85 multipartite instances, 15 gateway instances, all 59,808 semicomplete digraphs of orders 2–5 (52,528 strong), and the bidirected Petersen graph.
